key_insight: Hessian degeneracy shapes continuous-time AdamW’s long-run behavior: isolated critical points with nullity at most one yield convergence, while two degenerate directions can permit bounded persistent motion.
engineering_relevance: The results offer a geometric lens for reasoning about AdamW stability, showing that even strict convexity need not guarantee convergence in continuous time.
method: Analyze continuous-time AdamW with bias correction and fixed positive weight decay.
Establish global well-posedness and boundedness under suitable assumptions and sufficiently small decay.
Relate limiting dynamics to locally invariant manifolds whose dimension matches Hessian nullity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees, a persistent-motion example for a smooth strictly convex objective with a unique minimum, and bounds on long-time proximity to the critical set as decay decreases.
watch_item: These conditional continuous-time results do not directly establish convergence or instability for discrete AdamW implementations.
paper_title: On the Convergence of Continuous-Time AdamW
